sentences.text: Arechia is considered the oldest known genus of stingaree.
Researchers separated males from females, placing the latter in the genus Merabatis.
The species A. arambourgi honors Camille Arambourg, who first identified the teeth in 1952.
The genus was formally described by Cappetta in 1983.
Isolated teeth have been found in Senegal, Tunisia, and potentially Egypt.
The environment where A. crassicaudata lived matches the typical warm, shallow habitat of modern stingarees.
Arechia inhabited the northern Tethys Ocean during the Early Eocene.
Its existence spanned a period between 59.24 and 37.71 million years ago.
Some researchers suggest isolated teeth may date as late as the Early Oligocene, though this remains unconfirmed.
